description: pretooluse-author-field-audit.sh (via _hooklib.sh extract_author_fields, TOML mode) mis-parses the standard PEP 621 pyproject field authors = [{ name = "Denson Smith" }]: it extracts the malformed fragment '{ name = "Denson Smith' instead of the name 'Denson Smith', then denies the commit because that fragment is not in the principal-identity allow-list (which correctly holds denson / densonsmith2@gmail.com / Denson Smith). REPRO: hit live at the arc-77 commit on agents/secure-core/pyproject.toml (line 24: authors = [{ name = "Denson Smith" }]). The IDENTICAL line exists in agents/builder-deploy-core/pyproject.toml (line 20) but that file is already TRACKED (committed before the author-gate was armed), so the gate never scanned it — secure-core is the first PEP 621 pyproject committed under the armed gate, first to hit the bug. IMPACT: any new/edited pyproject.toml using the PEP 621 inline-table authors array (the standard form) is falsely blocked even when authorship is correct. CONCRETE FIX / next-step: extend extract_author_fields (TOML mode) in .claude/hooks/_hooklib.sh to parse the inline-table array form authors = [{ name = "X", email = "Y" }, ...] and emit each { name/email } value (like the JSON/YAML author paths already do), so the gate compares the real name against the allow-list; add a PEP 621 inline-table fixture to the author-gate test harness (relates stoa--eby drift-risk + stoa--p0e gate-extension). This is a substrate hook/tooling change -> requires its own arc (the-stoa: tooling source changes require an arc) + operator-gated (armed hook). Anchor: arc-77 commit blocker, stoa--po5.
